reading.body:
Kevin Mullin's AI record mixes grid and electricity bills with AI safety and research bills, and the same companies funding him also lobby on both.

The pattern is that AI policy for this member is not one subject. Two of the five bills he sponsored or cosponsored address electricity directly: the SHIELD Act on large load demands and the Affordable Innovation for the Grid Act. Two others address AI systems and their risks: the CHATBOT Act and the SAFE CROSS Act. The CREATE AI Act covers research resources. The committee money comes from Google, Meta, and Amazon PACs across five filings between May 2025 and July 2026, and the grid bills sit in the same window as those contributions.

That matters for AI because the binding constraint on scaling is power, and the legislative work that touches power is being done by the same members who write the AI rules. A reader tracking data center load growth has reason to watch the SHIELD Act and the grid bill as closely as the chatbot transparency bill, since one set of offices handles both.

What the data does not show is causation, and the page says so. Contributions and votes are listed in date order only. There is no record here of committee assignments, floor statements, or the text of any bill, so nothing indicates how Mullin voted on the grid measures or what the AI bills would do. The record covers 15 events and stops at October 2026.
